claim: CLRCH is the colour-RAM initialisation routine — the palette is written by the program, not read from a PROM.
CLRCH begins by loading the background colour byte from BKGND.
The background byte is stored into colour-RAM slot ANCOL+8.
Per-level colours are read out of the 99$ table, indexed 12 bytes per centipede level.
Colour-RAM slot ANCOL+5 is the inside-of-mushroom colour.
Colour-RAM slot ANCOL+6 is the outside-of-mushroom colour.
Motion-object colour-RAM slot MOCOL+1 is a centipede colour.
The immediate colour byte $1F is the programmers' RED — under the active-low wiring it drives only the three red lines.
The immediate colour byte $00 is the programmers' WHITE — every output line driven.
The 99$ per-level colour table opens with the CENTIN=1 row: mushroom inside/outside and DDT colours.
